EZ05e7EMOLM.summary: Ian Cooper's DevTernity talk revisits Kent Beck's original TDD ideas and shows where misunderstandings crept in. It argues tests should target behaviors through public interfaces rather than implementation details, so suites support refactoring instead of resisting it.
EZ05e7EMOLM.why: HN repeatedly calls it the best talk on testing, and many say it changed how they approach tests, mocks and the meaning of a unit.

ERbvKrH-GC4.summary: A two-minute animation of an Alan Watts talk arguing that life is like music: it is meant to be danced to in the moment, not rushed toward a final goal. It is a short, accessible take on living in the present.
ERbvKrH-GC4.why: HN commenters post it in threads about purpose, ambition, burnout and career anxiety as a reframing that life is a dance, not a march toward eventual happiness.

EY6q5dv_B-o.summary: Brian Kernighan interviews Unix co-creator Ken Thompson at VCF East 2019. Thompson recounts how he was hired at Bell Labs, writing the Unix kernel in about three weeks, the origins of B and TMG, pipes, and other anecdotes.
EY6q5dv_B-o.why: HN commenters recommend it for Thompson's funny, first-hand Unix history stories, some of which even Kernighan had not heard.

Erp8IAUouus.summary: CGP Grey explains the history of the US Social Security card and number, and why they became a de facto national ID despite never being meant for it. He also covers why America resists a proper identity card.
Erp8IAUouus.why: HN reaches for it in every identity theft and data breach thread as the clearest, most enjoyable short explainer of why SSNs make bad identifiers.

EYPapE-3FRw.summary: A short clip of Richard Feynman explaining the scientific method: guess, compute consequences, compare to experiment, and why vague theories like astrology cannot be proven wrong.
EYPapE-3FRw.why: Widely recommended as one of the clearest, funniest short explanations of what makes something science.

EKWGGDXe5MA.summary: A lecture by Richard Feynman on how computers work, using the analogy of a filing clerk that becomes progressively dumber and faster. It also covers heuristics and how computers handle data and solve problems in finite time.
EKWGGDXe5MA.why: Frequently recommended as the clearest plain-language explanation of what a computer fundamentally is, with at least one commenter saying it changed how they think about programming.

EiZhdpLXZ8Q.summary: Dan Olson of Folding Ideas spends months in the virtual world Decentraland and delivers a long critique of the metaverse, NFTs and DAOs, and why virtual worlds fail as places.
EiZhdpLXZ8Q.why: Regarded as the definitive takedown of the metaverse hype and the Decentraland ecosystem.

Eq3bUFgEcb4.summary: Tantacrul's 76-minute deep dive into the history of western music notation and the many proposed replacements, such as piano rolls, colored notes and the jubilate. He explains why none have displaced the current system.
Eq3bUFgEcb4.why: Repeatedly recommended as the definitive, well-made explanation of why attempts to reinvent music notation fail and what tradeoffs the current system makes.

ELeZAKCN4tY.summary: Herb Sutter's CppCon 2022 talk on whether C++ can become ten times simpler and safer. He introduces his experimental Cpp2 syntax and the cppfront transpiler, explaining the limits on incremental improvement.
ELeZAKCN4tY.why: HN recommends it as the main introduction to Cpp2 and cppfront, and as a credible effort to evolve C++.

EK32jo7i5LQ.summary: 3Blue1Brown explains why plotting primes in polar coordinates produces spiral patterns, using modular arithmetic, Dirichlet's theorem and rational approximations of pi.
EK32jo7i5LQ.why: Frequently recommended as the clearest explanation of prime spirals and the Ulam spiral.

Eco2s3-0zsQ.summary: A Joe Rogan podcast with retired Navy commander David Fravor, who describes his 2004 Tic Tac UFO encounter, and filmmaker Jeremy Corbell. Fravor walks through the incident and the released videos.
Eco2s3-0zsQ.why: HN refers to it as the direct first-person account from the pilot in UFO and UAP threads, though some find it unconvincing.

En_2T7KH6RA.summary: Ted Nelson demonstrates Xanadu Space, his software for representing hypertext in three-dimensional space with linked, referenced content fragments.
En_2T7KH6RA.why: Recommended as the shortest way to grasp Nelson's idea of referential content and how the web could have been different.

ExgxwKnH8y4.summary: ReasonTV tells the story of Bob Tillman, who spent nearly five years and $1.4 million trying to convert his San Francisco laundromat into apartments. It walks through the permitting, appeals and neighborhood opposition he faced.
ExgxwKnH8y4.why: It is HN's go-to concrete example of how local regulation and NIMBYism block new housing in San Francisco and California.

EOwxxsPaogY.summary: FortNine explains how Harley-Davidson ended up in decline, from a narrow lifestyle niche and an aging customer base to the pandemic hitting a company already in trouble.
EOwxxsPaogY.why: Recommended as an entertaining overview of Harley's decline and as a case study in selling a lifestyle rather than a product.

EWX5B6cD4_4.summary: Myst co-creator Rand Miller recounts how the HyperCard-built game struggled to run on 1x CD-ROM drives. He and his brother Robyn compressed image and audio data heavily to get acceptable performance. Part of Ars Technica's War Stories series.
EWX5B6cD4_4.why: HN commenters point to it as the first-person story of how Myst grew out of HyperCard and fit on CD-ROM, especially in threads about HyperCard and retro game constraints.

E0W1ZZYIV8o.summary: David MacKay's TEDxWarwick talk uses basic arithmetic to show how much land and energy renewables would need to power a country like the UK. It explains the limits of sustainable options and why they should still be pursued.
E0W1ZZYIV8o.why: Cited in energy debates for its back-of-envelope scale of the transition and the land and storage limits of wind and solar.

EUXnJraKM3k.summary: A 2006 parody made by a Microsoft team that shows how the company would redesign iPod packaging, with a box piled with feature claims, logos and clutter in contrast to Apple's clean design.
EUXnJraKM3k.why: HN commenters bring it up whenever Microsoft product naming, branding or marketing is confusing, pointing to it as a long-running self-aware critique.

Ecy1FBdCRbQ.summary: The Lock Picking Lawyer tests the supposedly unpickable lock designs built by the Stuff Made Here channel. He looks for bypasses and weaknesses in the novel anti-picking mechanisms.
Ecy1FBdCRbQ.why: HN points to it in lock-security threads as a good example of engineering meeting real-world exploitation, where flaws unrelated to the headline mechanism get found.

Eghl19elKk8.summary: Historian Timothy Snyder explains the politics of inevitability and the politics of eternity, two ways of thinking about time that frame his books On Tyranny and The Road to Unfreedom.
Eghl19elKk8.why: Recommended as a short, clear introduction to these two concepts for making sense of current politics.

E8Lhqri8tZk.summary: In this 2019 GDC talk, Alex Schwartz and Ziba Scott explain how they flooded the app stores with over 1,500 auto-generated slot machine games to find the lowest bar for success. They tour the dark side of the mobile app market.
E8Lhqri8tZk.why: HN commenters recommend it as a hilarious account of mass-produced app store shovelware and cite it in threads on spam and low-quality content.

EBCYvoC4muc.summary: Linus Akesson demonstrates the Commodordion, a fully functional 8-bit accordion built around Commodore 64 hardware with bellows made of floppy disks. He performs Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag and tells the story of the build.
EBCYvoC4muc.why: HN people recommend it as the work of an unusually creative artist-engineer whose whole channel is worth exploring.

EZxP0i9ah8E.summary: Paul Buchheit, creator of Gmail and founder of FriendFeed, speaks at Startup School 08 about listening to users. He covers feedback, features, aiming for 100 happy users, and treating "that's impossible" as a statement of limited experience.
EZxP0i9ah8E.why: HN commenters cite it for its memorable lines on advice, limited experience and early user focus, and rewatch it as a reminder not to be prescriptive.

E_xCssR8qQI.summary: A Blender-animated explanation of the Toyota Hybrid Synergy Drive, showing how the engine, two motor-generators, planetary gearset and battery work together as an eCVT.
E_xCssR8qQI.why: HN recommends it as the clearest visual explanation of how the Prius power-split hybrid actually works.

Ee3EtYb8d1o.summary: Day 1 of Casey Muratori's Handmade Hero, a live-coded game built from scratch in C on Windows. It reviews C on Windows, sets up a minimal build system and WinMain entry point, and shows a first MessageBox.
Ee3EtYb8d1o.why: HN recommends the series as a thorough look at low-level game programming by someone with deep knowledge, offered free.

EfGD2qveGdQ.summary: A short smartphone-recorded clip from a 2014 event in Paris where DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis presents an AI learning to play old Atari games. The system learns from only the video signal and the score. Audio quality is poor.
EfGD2qveGdQ.why: HN commenters use it as the canonical demo of deep reinforcement learning, noting that watching it teaches more than an article does.

EgiMu8A3pi0.summary: A very long, detailed look at the A4/V2 rocket turbopump, the steam-turbine-driven twin propellant pump system. It covers the peroxide and permanganate catalysis that drives the turbine. This is part 1 of a series on V2 components.
EgiMu8A3pi0.why: HN commenters recommend the series for its in-depth, hands-on explanation of how V2 turbopumps and peroxide decomposition work.

EmKQsSDlaa4.summary: 3Blue1Brown explains how holograms record a 3D scene on 2D film, using wave diffraction and phase. The video includes demonstrations of several real holograms.
EmKQsSDlaa4.why: HN commenters call it the best explanation of how holograms work, and one says it transformed their understanding.

EoWMF3VkI6U.summary: Afrotechmods plays with 2600F ultracapacitors that can dump hundreds of amps, shorting them to vaporize bits of metal. Along the way he explains the three most important capacitor equations. The uploader warns that the capacitors are not designed to be shorted.
EoWMF3VkI6U.why: HN commenters use it as a vivid, math-backed demonstration of what ultracapacitors can do and why shorting them is dangerous.

Ep2-ohgFOys.summary: A Soho Forum debate in which patent lawyer Stephan Kinsella argues for abolishing copyright and patents against law professor Richard Epstein. Both come from libertarian perspectives.
Ep2-ohgFOys.why: HN points to it as a substantive debate on intellectual property from two libertarian angles, with Kinsella as the abolitionist voice.

EGqwXt90ZqA.summary: Bret Victor's talk from Dropbox's DBX conference about living by a guiding principle, in his case that creators need an immediate connection to what they are making. He shows live-coding and time-manipulation demos that let ideas take form at the speed of thought.
EGqwXt90ZqA.why: HN commenters cite it as the best demonstration of why instant feedback matters in programming tools.

EMKLeS-Uq_8.summary: The old announcement trailer for Hyperbolica, CodeParade's Unity game set in hyperbolic and spherical space. The creator has since posted devlog videos on building it.
EMKLeS-Uq_8.why: Pointed to when non-Euclidean geometry or games in hyperbolic space come up, along with the creator's well-liked devlog.

ESXOAJRdcwQ.summary: George Hotz gives a SXSW 2019 talk on the idea that we live in a simulation and asks what actions would be available from inside it. He takes a hacker's view of whether it could be escaped.
ESXOAJRdcwQ.why: Shared in simulation-argument threads as an entertaining, hacker-minded take, though some commenters criticize Hotz himself.

E8T_4zqWmq8.summary: A one-hour OCaml Workshop 2020 talk on the state of the OCaml Platform, covering IDE support, next steps for the tooling and plans for 2020-2021.
E8T_4zqWmq8.why: HN points to it as the latest progress report on OCaml tooling and the community push to improve the platform.

EIezuL_doYw.summary: Climate Town's comedic explainer on carbon offsets and whether companies can buy their way out of climate change. It argues that offsets won't save us, while granting they are not bad in principle.
EIezuL_doYw.why: HN shares it as an entertaining, well-argued critique of carbon offsetting in threads on greenwashing.

ENLWEfi0Tkg.summary: Rob Pike presents Upspin at Gopherfest 2017, an experimental framework for naming and sharing files and data securely and uniformly across a global namespace. It is a project written in Go rather than about Go.
ENLWEfi0Tkg.why: Cited as the talk that introduced Upspin, and called fascinating and really good by commenters.

EQs5VxNPhzk.summary: Neural-network upscaled, 60 fps, stabilized and colorized version of 1902 footage of the Wuppertal Schwebebahn suspended railway in Germany. The source film comes from MoMA. It gives a vivid view of an early-1900s city and a train system that still runs.
EQs5VxNPhzk.why: HN commenters share it as a favorite example of upscaled vintage footage that makes the early 1900s feel present, though some find the colorization off.

E_F5GxCwizc.summary: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on native advertising, showing how ads are disguised as editorial content in news media, including BuzzFeed and major newspapers.
E_F5GxCwizc.why: Recommended as a funny, clear explanation of native advertising whenever sponsored content in media is discussed.

Ed3ioGO7g10.summary: Developmental and synthetic biologist Michael Levin speaks at a Harvard Extension student event on bioelectricity, body intelligence and regenerative medicine. He discusses how cell electrical networks guide growth and form.
Ed3ioGO7g10.why: Recommended as an approachable look at Levin's work on regrowth and collective cellular intelligence, and used as an example of intelligence beyond brains.

EhqZ0RU95d4.summary: Gary Vaynerchuk's Web 2.0 Expo keynote on building a personal brand in social media. He urges keeping a day job while building something on the side, with passion and persistence, in a loud and profane style.
EhqZ0RU95d4.why: Recommended in Ask HN career threads as motivational advice to use spare hours to start building.

ExwqNreocpg.summary: MattKC fits a playable Snake game into a QR code by writing tiny x86 machine code and patching the ZBar scanner so it can run the decoded data.
ExwqNreocpg.why: HN admires it as a creative hack and cites it as the inspiration for later tiny-game and QR-code projects.

E4tYpXVTjxA.summary: Disney Research presents Touche, a swept frequency capacitive sensing technique that recognizes complex hand and body configurations, and adds touch sensitivity to humans, liquids and everyday objects.
E4tYpXVTjxA.why: Brought up as an early example of context-aware touch sensing and as part of Disney Research's wider interaction prototypes.

EACkiMRT0pc.summary: Practical Engineering explains what a 100-year flood actually means, combining statistics, hydrology and how society treats risk. Grady walks through local drainage infrastructure and the caveats in estimating flood probability.
EACkiMRT0pc.why: HN points to it as a clear explanation of what flood return periods really mean.

EH6vE97qIP4.summary: The opening lecture of MIT's Blockchain and Money course taught by Gary Gensler, covering the course plan, the history of failed digital currencies, cryptography and what a blockchain is.
EH6vE97qIP4.why: Recommended as a solid, level-headed academic introduction to blockchain, often noted because Gensler later led the SEC.

EL7Au1tzNxE.summary: Jon Gjengset spends about three hours livecoding complex changes in a Rust codebase with agentic AI tools, testing his hypothesis that AI is weak at non-pattern work. He documents where Claude Code helps and where it struggles.
EL7Au1tzNxE.why: Pointed to as a non-promotional, realistic long session of an experienced engineer working with AI on non-trivial code.

EP9F-AZezCU.summary: Day9 gives a passionate first look at what his StarCraft: Brood War Remastered series will teach. He argues Brood War is primarily a real-time game and only secondarily a strategy game, making the commander fantasy a matter of mechanics.
EP9F-AZezCU.why: HN uses it to argue that mechanical difficulty and limited attention are integral to RTS strategy, especially in StarCraft AI threads.

EcKxaq1FTac.summary: The 1990 NOVA documentary follows astronomer Clifford Stoll as he tracks a hacker through military and research computer networks, a story that involved the CIA and KGB. It is based on The Cuckoo's Egg.
EcKxaq1FTac.why: HN lists it among favorite nerdy documentaries and enjoys hearing Stoll tell the story himself.

EeYvFl7li9E.summary: Ryan Dahl's JSConf EU talk introducing Node.js to the world. He explains the motivation for event-driven, non-blocking I/O, with JavaScript chosen mainly for its asynchronous nature.
EeYvFl7li9E.why: Cited as the primary source for why Node exists and why JavaScript was chosen, in debates about async models and language choice.

EfjdOc41g0s.summary: A NANOG 64 panel with speakers from Comcast, APNIC, T-Mobile and Facebook on deploying IPv6-only networks, including performance data showing IPv6 outperforming NAT-ed IPv4.
EfjdOc41g0s.why: Cited as real operator data that IPv6 is faster than IPv4 and that large networks are already going IPv6-only.

EgMqhEMhVV8.summary: The Game Theorists analyze how PewDiePie rose to become the most subscribed channel on YouTube. The video looks at why let's plays and gaming channels thrive on the platform.
EgMqhEMhVV8.why: HN commenters cite it as an analysis of PewDiePie's popularity and of how YouTube's recommendations favored gaming content.

Eg_ToU7m1MI.summary: Alan Kay's TED talk on teaching ideas, in which he argues the world is not what it seems and shows children learning through programming and building their own lessons with Etoys/Squeak.
Eg_ToU7m1MI.why: Recommended as a condensed version of Kay's ideas on education and computing, showing kids using software to explore physics and robotics.

EkpQAGQiv4Q.summary: A long rebuttal arguing that the Wright Brothers truly invented the airplane, responding to other YouTubers who credit others. It walks through the engineering breakthroughs the Wrights achieved, such as control and wind tunnel work.
EkpQAGQiv4Q.why: HN commenters use it as a well-researched account of what the Wrights actually solved, in threads on airplane physics and invention credit.

Em7nqDqQ8oM.summary: Charles Marohn of Strong Towns presents, in a Talks at Google session, the ideas from his book on why many North American towns struggle financially despite decades of growth. He argues for incremental, bottom-up city building as a path to local prosperity.
Em7nqDqQ8oM.why: HN commenters link it in housing and urbanism threads as a clear explanation of unsustainable car-oriented development and fragile systems.

EpRrD58Ah3Q.summary: Dr. Michael Greger gives a live presentation on evidence-based weight loss, previewing his book How Not to Diet. He focuses on foods that aid weight loss while also supporting health and longevity.
EpRrD58Ah3Q.why: HN commenters share it as a helpful lecture on plant-based weight loss and which foods to experiment with.

EuELwq2ThJE.summary: A Google Tech Talk arguing that the best interface requires the fewest clicks and choices, with Google search, Facebook, the iPod and Firefox as examples. It shows how minimizing interaction makes interfaces easier to learn.
EuELwq2ThJE.why: HN commenters recommend it as a companion to Steve Krug's usability advice and as a talk on minimal interface design.

Ev373c7wSRg.summary: A short comedy skit by Ryan Long satirizing how woke activists and racists end up agreeing on many things.
Ev373c7wSRg.why: Posted as relevant satire in threads on wokeness and identity politics, with some saying it is barely an exaggeration.

E2MIpi8pIvY.summary: John Romero's 2016 GDC Europe talk recounts the early days of id Software and the programming principles behind Doom and Quake, including fast iteration and keeping the game bootable.
E2MIpi8pIvY.why: Strongly recommended as an inspiring hour on how id worked, often linked in programming-practice threads.

E3URhJx0NSw.summary: Joe Rogan interviews epidemiologist Michael Osterholm in March 2020 about the coronavirus. They cover how it spreads, masks, hygiene, social distancing, school closures and vaccine timelines.
E3URhJx0NSw.why: During early Covid, HN recommended it as an in-depth, informed explanation of transmission and outbreak dynamics.

E8V8rtdXnLA.summary: A talk given at the 2011 Nammour Symposium at Sacramento State arguing that past generations were wrong about nearly everything, so we should expect to be wrong too. It tours the many surprising ways scientific beliefs have failed, drawing on pessimistic induction.
E8V8rtdXnLA.why: HN uses it as a reference for epistemic humility and how wrong even the smartest people have been.

E9KJ_f7REGw.summary: Hobbyist Wesley Kagan shows his Miata running and driving with a homemade version of Koenigsegg's freevalve camless valve technology. The build uses open CAD files and code and he describes it as an ongoing work in progress.
E9KJ_f7REGw.why: HN commenters cite it as an impressive hobbyist project and as an example of open-source engine control enabling freevalve retrofits.

EUrOxh_0leE.summary: Physicist and YouTuber Angela Collier argues in this hour-long video that AI as commonly described does not really exist. She covers the limits of the tools, biased datasets, and why they should not be used to make decisions.
EUrOxh_0leE.why: HN people point to it as a clear, skeptical take on AI hype and the risks of unreliable AI classification, such as in mushroom foraging books.

E1AxVXt2Gv4.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Marcus Hutter of DeepMind about universal artificial intelligence, AIXI, Kolmogorov complexity, Solomonoff induction and the idea of intelligence as compression.
E1AxVXt2Gv4.why: Referenced as an accessible explanation of Kolmogorov complexity and Hutter's view of intelligence as compression.

E3p_Cv32tEo.summary: Technology Connections takes apart the step-by-step electromechanical logic of a 1970s pinball machine. He shows how relays, steppers and switches track state and score without electronics.
E3p_Cv32tEo.why: HN recommends it as an in-depth look at mechanical logic, and uses it as an analogy for state machines and biological instruction processing.

E5pZ7uR6v8c.summary: A short video of a man moving a 20 ton stone block by himself using wood and levers. It is part of a pyramid-mysteries channel.
E5pZ7uR6v8c.why: HN cites it as a hands-on demonstration that one person with simple tools can move huge stones, undercutting arguments that ancient construction needed lost technology.

E7MQb9Y4FAE.summary: Tim Dodd of Everyday Astronaut gets a close-up walkthrough of SpaceX's Raptor 2 engine from Elon Musk at Starbase. They cover how Raptor 2 was simplified and upgraded relative to Raptor 1, including cooling and thrust vectoring details.
E7MQb9Y4FAE.why: HN points to it as a rare, detailed first-person explanation of Raptor engine design from Musk himself.

E8kUJL04ELA.summary: John Conway talks in a short Numberphile interview about his mixed feelings toward the Game of Life, his most famous invention. He says he is not especially pleased that it overshadowed his other work.
E8kUJL04ELA.why: Cited whenever commenters want to note that Conway did not enjoy being known mainly for the Game of Life.

EESYomdoeCs.summary: A Bloomberg documentary on how Boeing's failures around the 737 Max crashes followed a shift in company culture and cost-cutting. It covers the grounding, the stock drop and questions about the company's future.
EESYomdoeCs.why: Cited as a source for Boeing's post-merger cultural decline and the undermining of its engineers.

EFRUL7vKdU8.summary: Randall Munroe of xkcd answers what would happen if you swam in a spent nuclear fuel pool, and how much radiation you would receive at the surface versus at depth.
EFRUL7vKdU8.why: Recommended whenever a thread asks how dangerous it is to fall into a reactor or fuel pool.

ET_b78GSBUs.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on how prosecutors wield power in the US criminal justice system and how it can be abused. It touches on elected district attorneys, plea pressure and the lack of electoral competition.
ET_b78GSBUs.why: HN cites it as an accessible explainer of prosecutorial abuse, especially piling on charges to force plea deals.

EUWVVTY63hc.summary: Gamers Nexus benchmarks how the amount and application method of thermal paste affect CPU cooling. It compares pea-sized dots, thin spreads and large blobs with Thermal Grizzly Kryonaut.
EUWVVTY63hc.why: HN cites it as data that too much thermal paste is mostly a myth and that too little is the real risk.

EWqThb9Z1jk.summary: A look at how granite surface plates are inspected, calibrated and reconditioned using an autocollimator, a repeat meter and diamond-charged cast iron laps. Measurements are at the level of millionths of an inch.
EWqThb9Z1jk.why: Cited in threads on flatness and precision as a glimpse into a niche metrology profession.

Ea6tw-gulnQ.summary: Technology Connections follows up on his analog TV video to clear up the debate over whether CRT phosphor dots are pixels. He explains the shadow mask, color triads and how they relate to the scanned picture.
Ea6tw-gulnQ.why: HN links it whenever someone equates CRT phosphors with pixels, as the clear explanation of why they are not.

EczW2IWdnOM.summary: Tim Ansell presents the SkyWater PDK, a fully open source manufacturable process development kit for a 130nm process, as the first FOSSi Dial-Up talk. He covers its role in a fully open chip design flow.
EczW2IWdnOM.why: HN commenters point to it for Google's reasons for backing open silicon and for background on the open-source chip design workflow.

Ef-mxjYkllw.summary: Isaac Arthur explains the Matrioshka Brain, a hypothetical computer or artificial mind powered by an entire star using nested shells. It covers how such megastructures relate to Dyson spheres and superintelligence.
Ef-mxjYkllw.why: HN points to it as the accessible introduction to Matrioshka Brains whenever very large computational structures come up.

EtX7WnFhxtQ.summary: A Remedy engineer explains how Alan Wake 2 moved to a GPU-driven rendering pipeline built on mesh shaders, culling and rendering meshlets for dense vegetation on PS5 and Xbox Series consoles.
EtX7WnFhxtQ.why: HN points to it as a detailed production example of mesh shaders and GPU-driven rendering, though some find it daunting.

EtsXgODHMWk.summary: MIT Media Lab shows an imaging system capturing a trillion frames per second, fast enough to film light pulses travelling through objects in slow motion.
EtsXgODHMWk.why: HN cites it as the original and still-wow reference whenever newer ultra-high-speed light imaging comes up.

E3s-qZsjK8I.summary: A short stand-up bit from Bill Burr at Night of Too Many Stars 2012, mocking Steve Jobs and the reverence surrounding him.
E3s-qZsjK8I.why: Shared as a joke in Steve Jobs and Apple threads as a funny counterpoint to the Jobs hagiography.

E7kor5nHtZQ.summary: Short 2006 footage of station staff in white gloves pushing commuters onto a packed morning train at a Tokyo station on the Toyoko Line.
E7kor5nHtZQ.why: Linked as the standard illustration of Tokyo's rush-hour crowding whenever commuting and density come up.

EBxgrr0wL8M.summary: A two-minute classroom scene from the film Starship Troopers in which a teacher lectures on why only veterans earn the right to vote, titled Failure of Democracy.
EBxgrr0wL8M.why: HN commenters cite it as an example of the film's satire of militarism and fascist propaganda delivered deadpan.

ECwHZlvvVH4.summary: The question-and-answer session that followed Jonathan Blow's talk on dealing with lack of motivation, malaise and depression. It is hosted on YouTube as a mirror of a Twitch recording.
ECwHZlvvVH4.why: Mostly shared as a more reliable YouTube mirror, and cited as a related talk on motivation; one commenter criticizes Blow's comments on impostor syndrome.

EEh01PX-q9I.summary: Tech Ingredients builds a pair of large Voigt speakers and explains ported, transmission line and horn designs. It tests them in an anechoic chamber and uses constrained layer damping for the enclosure.
EEh01PX-q9I.why: Cited as a DIY speaker reference when commenters discuss building their own audio gear.

EGTRX6pZSns.summary: Thunderf00t critiques the MIT and Berkeley metal-organic framework device that claims to pull water from air using only solar heating. He argues the energy accounting does not work and that such devices are essentially fancy dehumidifiers.
EGTRX6pZSns.why: HN uses it as the standard debunking to cite whenever a new water-from-air device is announced.

EGUZJVY-sHo.summary: Top Gear segment in which Richard Hammond drives a Renault R25 Formula 1 car around Silverstone for two laps. He struggles with the car's demands.
EGUZJVY-sHo.why: HN cites it as an illustration of how hard F1 cars are to drive, for example that they can't go slowly because of no downforce or tyre heat.

EHqPrHTN1dU.summary: A short Google Japan promotional video, in Japanese, for Gboard Double-Sided, a keyboard with no back side that comes in a paper-craft version and a full electronics version. It is a playful April-Fools-style product concept.
EHqPrHTN1dU.why: HN mentions it mainly as an example of Google Japan's habit of making joke keyboards, with some complaints that it was misleading.

EIyixC9NsLI.summary: The classic MrWeebl animated music video Badgers, a short looping song of badgers, a mushroom and a snake. It is a staple of early internet absurdist humor.
EIyixC9NsLI.why: HN invokes it purely as a joke or nostalgic meme reference.

ELCq63652ig.summary: TechAltar's eight-minute video arguing that Chrome is becoming the new Internet Explorer as Google leverages its browser position. It covers anti-competitive behavior toward other browsers like Firefox and Edge and the role of Chromium.
ELCq63652ig.why: HN commenters cite it as a good example of how Google treats browsers that are not Chrome and of the browser-monopoly concern.

EPk8MVEmiTI.summary: A one-minute demo at the Computer History Museum's IBM 1401 restoration lab, where a program makes the machine's radio-frequency interference play tunes on an AM radio.
EPk8MVEmiTI.why: HN cites it as the classic early example of a computer producing music through electromagnetic emissions, in threads on System Bus Radio and similar hacks.

EShUeudtaFg.summary: A short comedy video reading out a famously misspelled Yahoo! Answers question about pregnancy over music.
EShUeudtaFg.why: Referenced as a legendary internet joke, usually when misspellings or Yahoo Answers come up.

EZD3Scuv02g.summary: Guy Steele's JuliaCon 2016 keynote on the Fortress language, its features and the lessons learned from the project.
EZD3Scuv02g.why: Cited as the authoritative first-hand account of the Fortress experience and of numerical computing language design.

Ec4NgWRE8ik.summary: A 34C3 talk on the security architecture of the Nintendo Switch and the early progress breaking it. It introduces the Switch's custom OS and software stack, with the hackers' reverse-engineering and glitching work.
Ec4NgWRE8ik.why: Used as a reference for how the Switch was actually broken, including the Tegra debug backdoor, and for facts about its non-FreeBSD kernel.

Ecvv-EvOj8M.summary: Berkeley neuroscientist Jack Gallant shows how fMRI brain mapping can be used to decode what a person sees, with visualizations of brain activity and its implications.
Ecvv-EvOj8M.why: HN cites it in discussions of reconstructing images from brain scans and the ethics of future brain reading.

Ej0sss6cq14.summary: Stuart Marks explains the intended purpose and proper use of Java 8's Optional class and why it caused so much controversy. He gives guidelines for using its small API correctly.
Ej0sss6cq14.why: Cited as the authoritative explanation, from the person who added it to OpenJDK, of Optional's narrow intended purpose.

EjmtSkl53h4.summary: An 8-minute clip of George Carlin's 1992 stand-up bit on the environment, arguing the planet will be fine and it is people who are in trouble. It leans on the contrast between Earth's 4.5 billion years and humanity's 200,000.
EjmtSkl53h4.why: Commenters cite it as shorthand for the view that the Earth will outlast us, usually as a quip rather than a recommendation.

EozPi1qmH44.summary: Louis Rossmann reacts to lobbyist ads in the Massachusetts right-to-repair ballot fight that suggest repair access would enable domestic abuse and discrimination, and urges support for the campaign.
EozPi1qmH44.why: HN mentions it mainly as an example of the manufacturer-backed arguments used against right to repair.

ErpNpR3XYUw.summary: A short 2012 promotional-style video of Google Glass showing what the headset was meant to do. It shows features like map directions and overlays in the wearer's view.
ErpNpR3XYUw.why: Cited as an example of what Glass promised, for comparison with later AR glasses.

ErwS24cBZPc.summary: A 4K upscaled restoration of Apple's 1984 Macintosh Super Bowl ad directed by Ridley Scott. The restoration combines various sources and an AI upscaler.
ErwS24cBZPc.why: Not recommended as a watch; HN cites the ad as shorthand for orderly conformity and as an example of an ad that has aged badly.

ExWfh6sGyso.summary: The classic 'What have the Romans ever done for us?' scene from Monty Python's Life of Brian, in which revolutionaries grudgingly list the benefits of Roman rule. It is a short comedy clip.
ExWfh6sGyso.why: HN commenters mostly drop it as a joke when someone downplays the upsides of something, such as a platform, a company or industrialization.

ExaAYIKsDBI.summary: A one-minute clip of Sony's keynote at E3 1995, where Steve Race takes the stage, announces the PlayStation's $299 price and leaves. It followed Sega's Saturn announcement at a higher price.
ExaAYIKsDBI.why: Cited as shorthand for one of the most effective moments in console marketing and for how a price announcement can sink a rival.

EzTWjNUb4H4.summary: Wells Fargo engineers walk through the bank's four-year IPv6 journey at the North American IPv6 Summit 2014. They cover motivation, approach, achievements and observations.
EzTWjNUb4H4.why: HN cites it in IPv6 threads as an example of a large adopter, especially for address-space collisions after mergers and conflicts in 10/8.

EzZGPCyrpSU.summary: PBS Space Time surveys five realistic options for interstellar travel, from conventional rocket fuel to antimatter and nuclear pulse propulsion. The options rely only on known physics.
EzZGPCyrpSU.why: HN commenters link it in propulsion and space threads as an episode on interstellar travel that needs no unknown physics.
